meta.description: Unified Python interface to 40+ bioinformatics services. Use when querying multiple databases (UniProt, KEGG, ChEMBL, Reactome) in a single workflow with consistent API. Best for cross-database analysis, ID mapping across services. For quick single-database lookups use gget; for sequence/file manipulation use biopython.

scientific_integrity.detail: No fabricated identifiers or data. All examples use valid protein IDs and standard bioinformatics operations.

practice_boundaries.detail: Database access wrapper skill, no medical claims or clinical recommendations.

methodological_ground.detail: Cross-database mapping and pathway analysis patterns follow established bioinformatics workflows.

code_usability.detail: All code examples syntactically correct with proper error handling patterns.

functional_suitability.note: Complete coverage of multi-database integration use cases. Examples accurate and appropriate for cross-service workflows.

reliability.note: Asynchronous BLAST patterns documented. Error handling shown but could be more comprehensive across all services.

performance_context.note: Excellent progressive disclosure with 360-line SKILL.md and 3 focused reference files. Efficient organization by service type.

agent_usability.note: Clear service-based organization. Consistent patterns across services. Good feedback design with status checking for async operations.

human_usability.note: Natural trigger language for cross-database tasks. Clear scope boundaries distinguishing from gget and biopython.

security.note: Email requirement documented for NCBI services. No credential exposure. Input validation delegated to service APIs.

maintainability.note: Clean modular separation by service type across 3 reference files. No formal test cases provided.

agent_specific.note: Good trigger precision and composability. Progressive disclosure effective. Escape hatches present with gget/biopython boundaries.

inputs.label: UniProt search with KEGG pathway mapping
inputs.note: Excellent integration showing UniProt search, FASTA retrieval, KEGG mapping, and pathway discovery

assertions.note: Correct frmt and columns parameters for tabular output

key_strengths: Excellent scope definition distinguishing from gget (quick lookups) and biopython (file manipulation)
Strong cross-database integration examples showing UniProt-KEGG-ChEMBL workflows
Clear service organization with 40+ services grouped by functionality type
Good handling of asynchronous operations with status checking patterns
Effective progressive disclosure with focused reference files for specific workflow types

recommendations.title: Add comprehensive error handling patterns
recommendations.problem: Error handling mentioned but not demonstrated consistently across all service types.
recommendations.root_cause: Focus on successful workflows without extensive failure mode coverage.
recommendations.fix: Add error handling section to each reference file covering: network timeouts, invalid IDs, service unavailability, rate limiting, empty result sets with retry strategies.

recommendations.title: Document rate limiting for different services
recommendations.problem: NCBI email requirement documented but rate limits for other services not explicitly covered.
recommendations.root_cause: Service-specific rate limits not consolidated in one location.
recommendations.fix: Add rate limiting reference section documenting: requests per second for each major service, batch size recommendations, exponential backoff patterns for retries.

recommendations.title: Add service availability and fallback guidance
recommendations.problem: No guidance on handling service outages or using alternative services for same data type.
recommendations.fix: Add service alternatives table showing: which services provide similar data types, when to use local vs remote BLAST, fallback strategies when primary service unavailable.
